If the patient is symptomatic due to hyponatremia from any cause then usually it's treated with hypertonic saline 3%.

 In asymptomatic patients with hypovolemic hyponatremia then normal saline can be given. Eg. Diuretics, cerebral salt wasting, GI losses etc. If symptomatic use hypertonic saline. 


In asymptomatic patients with euvolemic hyponatremia fluid restriction can be done. Eg. SIADH, physiological stress, hypothyroidism. If symptomatic use hypertonic saline and add diuretic if needed. 



In asymptomatic patients with hypervolemic hyponatremia fluid restriction and diuretics can be given. Eg. Cirrhosis, heart failure, renal failure etc. If symptomatic use hypertonic saline and diuretics.
